articles.summary: Newly-released bodycam footage shows the moment troops detained 'El Chapo Isidro', who had managed to evade capture for years.
articles.body:
Newly-released bodycam footage shows the moment troops entered a house and detained a Mexican drug lord who had managed to evade capture for years.

The video shows armed personnel entering via a garage and finding Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, also known as 'El Chapo Isidro', who was on the FBI's most wanted list.

Seven suspects were killed in last Friday's operation, as were four members of the Mexican army who were travelling to reinforce security in Guasave, Mexico's defence secretariat said.

articles.title: O presente corporativo que o seu colaborador vai usar os 365 dias do ano | G1
articles.standfirst: CBA Cestas surpreende o mercado ao integrar mochilas originais da Wilson às composições festivas, provando que o reconhecimento não precisa acabar em dezembro.
articles.summary: CBA Cestas surpreende o mercado ao integrar mochilas originais da Wilson às composições festivas, provando que o reconhecimento não precisa acabar em dezembro.
articles.body:
O presente corporativo que o seu colaborador vai usar os 365 dias do ano — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação

A dinâmica das tradicionais cestas de Natal costuma seguir um roteiro previsível: em dezembro, a caixa chega repleta de expectativas. Na véspera da data, a família se reúne em torno da mesa farta. Em janeiro, as embalagens são descartadas e o presente se transforma apenas em uma boa memória. Mas e se o reconhecimento da empresa pudesse estar presente fisicamente na rotina do colaborador durante todo o ano seguinte?

Foi a partir dessa provocação que a CBA Cestas decidiu redefinir o conceito de durabilidade no mercado de presentes corporativos. Para a campanha deste ano, a empresa fechou uma parceria estratégica com a Wilson, marca globalmente reconhecida por sua excelência em artigos esportivos e utilitários. O resultado são composições exclusivas que trazem, junto à seleção premium de alimentos, uma mochila original da marca.

A inclusão da mochila altera por completo a percepção de valor do presente. Não se trata de uma "embalagem retornável" genérica ou de um brinde comum, mas de um acessório de alto padrão, desenhado para a vida real. É um item utilitário que transita com facilidade do escritório à academia, das viagens de fim de semana à sala de aula.

Para os departamentos de Recursos Humanos, a estratégia é um acerto cirúrgico. O presente corporativo deixa de ser efêmero e se transforma em um investimento de longo prazo no engajamento. "Quando a ceia acaba, a mochila fica", resume a premissa da novidade. Toda vez que o profissional arrumar sua mochila Wilson para sair de casa, ele carregará consigo a lembrança tangível da valorização de sua companhia, estendendo a vida útil da cesta de Natal por 365 dias.

Essa aposta na durabilidade, no entanto, não ofusca o brilho gastronômico da data. A mochila atua como o grande diferencial da temporada, mas chega muito bem acompanhada. As composições mantêm o rigor na curadoria dos alimentos, garantindo os clássicos indispensáveis para as festas de fim de ano, de panettones a espumantes, preservando as marcas renomadas que já são tradição na mesa do brasileiro.

Ao unir a magia imediata da ceia de Natal à longevidade de uma marca icônica como a Wilson, a CBA Cestas dá mais um passo à frente no setor. E prova, de forma incontestável, que os melhores presentes são aqueles que continuam sendo úteis muito tempo depois que as luzes de dezembro se apagam.

articles.title: Festival Vozes Delas começa com shows gratuitos no RN | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento tem entrada gratuita e passa por Natal, Mossoró e Lajes. Programação destaca o protagonismo feminino com shows de Daniela Mercury, Solange Almeida, Walkiria Santos e talentos locais.
articles.summary: O Festival Som de Verão - Vozes Delas começa nesta sexta (27) em Natal. Evento gratuito celebra a música feminina com shows de Daniela Mercury, Solange Almeida e artistas do RN.
articles.body:
Festival com Daniela Mercury, Khrystal e Solange Almeida celebra a música feminina no RN — Foto: Mateus Xavier/g1

O Festival Som de Verão - Vozes Delas começa nesta sexta-feira (27), na Praça Augusto Severo, em Natal, no Rio Grande do Norte. O evento com entrada gratuita tem o objetivo de celebrar o protagonismo das mulheres na música e promover o encontro entre diferentes gerações.

A cantora Daniela Mercury é a principal atração da noite de abertura. A programação na capital potiguar também conta com apresentações das artistas Bia Gurgel, Khrystal e Tetê Pessoa.

No sábado (28), o evento segue para Mossoró. Os shows ocorrem no espaço externo da Universidade Federal Rural do Semi-Árido (Ufersa). As atrações confirmadas para a data são Valéria Oliveira, Renata Falcão e Solange Almeida.

O encerramento do festival está marcado para o dia 11 de dezembro, no centro do município de Lajes. A última noite reúne as cantoras Rosas na Cartola, Deusa do Forró e Walkiria Santos.

O coordenador do festival, Dácio Galvão, afirma que o evento representa o reconhecimento da contribuição feminina para a cultura brasileira. "Estamos celebrando a potência criativa das mulheres, suas histórias e a diversidade de suas expressões musicais", disse.

Galvão também ressalta a importância de levar a programação para três cidades do estado. "O festival reúne artistas consagradas e talentos potiguares em uma programação que valoriza nossa identidade cultural e democratiza o acesso à música", afirmou o coordenador.

O evento é apresentado pelo Ministério da Cultura e pelo governo federal, com patrocínio da Petrobras por meio da Lei Rouanet. A realização é da Fundação José Augusto, da Secretaria de Estado da Cultura (Secult) e do governo do Rio Grande do Norte, com apoio da Secretaria de Estado do Turismo (Setur).

articles.title: WSJ: governo Trump negocia produção de drones militares com GM e Ford | G1
articles.standfirst: Pentágono lidera tratativas com a General Motors (GM) e a Ford, além de outras fabricantes, para ajudar na produção em larga escala de drones, segundo o 'The Wall Street Journal'.
articles.summary: Pentágono lidera tratativas com a General Motors (GM) e a Ford, além de outras fabricantes, para ajudar na produção em larga escala de drones, segundo o 'The Wall Street Journal'.
articles.body:
Drone militar MQ-9 Reaper, de função dupla de monitoramento e ataque, do Exército dos Estados Unidos. — Foto: Jam Sta Rosa/AFP

O Pentágono está em negociações com a General Motors (GM), a Ford e outras fabricantes automotivas para ajudar na produção em larga escala de drones militares, informou nesta terça-feira (24) o jornal norte-americano "The Wall Street Journal", citando pessoas familiarizadas com o assunto.

A indústria automobilística tem tentado aproveitar o aumento do governo Trump com os gastos em defesa, impulsionado por conflitos geopolíticos em todo o mundo, embora as oportunidades de ampliar a receita continuem limitadas, segundo analistas.

No acordo que está sendo negociado, as empresas forneceriam peças para fabricantes de drones, como atuadores, motores, sensores, sistemas de lidar e outros componentes, segundo a reportagem do WSJ.

A GM avalia a possibilidade de fabricar motores para drones , enquanto autoridades da área de Defesa dos EUA se reuniram com dirigentes da Ford, da fabricante canadense de autopeças Magna International e de outras empresas do setor industrial, algumas delas de fora da indústria automobilística, acrescentou a reportagem.

Segundo o WSJ, a GM demonstrou maior interesse em participar de projetos militares após solicitações de autoridades de alto escalão da área de defesa. A montadora também estaria em negociações com a RTX e a L3Harris para acordos semelhantes.

A GM também forneceu, no início deste ano, componentes de carcaças para os mísseis do sistema de defesa antiaérea Patriot, da Lockheed Martin, como parte de um acordo com a gigante do setor de defesa.

Ainda segundo o WSJ, nenhum acordo havia sido finalizado até o momento, e a iniciativa do governo do presidente Donald Trump recebeu reações divergentes de executivos da indústria automobilística.

O movimento ocorre em meio à guerra dos EUA contra o Irã, que já dura mais de nove meses sem perspectiva de ser finalizada e causou uma maior demanda —e em alguns casos até a escassez— por equipamentos militares como drones e mísseis. Nesse cenário, o governo Trump tem tomado medidas nos últimos meses para impulsionar a produção militar.

Nenhuma das montadoras citadas pela reportagem do WSJ havia se pronunciado sobre o assunto até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Prefeito de Seropédica é alvo de operação contra milícia de Tandera | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigação encontrou conversas de um policial militar com o miliciano sobre indicações para cargos públicos, uso de verbas municipais e lotação de policiais. Dois agentes da Draco também são investigados por vazamento de informações.
articles.summary: A Operação Simbiose do MPRJ investiga o prefeito de Seropédica, Professor Lucas, por suspeita de ceder cargos e verbas municipais à milícia liderada por Danilo Tandera.
articles.body:
O prefeito de Seropédica , Lucas Dutra dos Santos , o Professor Lucas ( PP ), é alvo de buscas nesta terça-feira (24) na Operação Simbiose , deflagrada pelo Ministério Público do Rio de Janeiro (MPRJ), que apura a interferência da milícia de Danilo Dias Lima , o Tandera , no município da Baixada Fluminense. Dois policiais, um civil e um militar, foram presos.

Promotores saíram para cumprir, no total, 3 mandados de prisão e 12 de busca e apreensão. Quatro dos mandados de busca foram expedidos pela Justiça a pedido do procurador-geral de Justiça, Antonio José Campos Moreira — os demais foram pelo Grupo de Atuação Especializada de Combate ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco/MPRJ).

Professor Lucas recebeu a equipe na porta de casa, descalço e com uma camisa de um time de futebol.

Equipes apreenderam nos endereços R$ 182 mil , armas, celulares, notebooks e mídias.

A TV Globo tenta contato com a defesa dos investigados.

Agentes do MPRJ acompanhados do prefeito de Seropédica, na Baixada Fluminense — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

A investigação começou com a análise do celular de um policial militar, apreendido pelo Gaeco durante uma investigação sobre a organização criminosa comandada por Tandera.

No aparelho, os investigadores encontraram diversas conversas entre o PM e o miliciano que apontam para a interferência do miliciano na administração de Seropédica. Entre os assuntos tratados estavam indicações para cargos públicos, utilização de verbas municipais e lotação de policiais na cidade .

No mesmo celular, os investigadores localizaram diálogos com 2 policiais civis da Delegacia de Repressão às Ações Criminosas Organizadas (Draco). Segundo a investigação, os agentes repassavam informações sobre operações policiais para Tandera .

O prefeito Professor Lucas teve o mandato cassado em maio por abuso de poder econômico nas eleições municipais de 2024. Ele, no entanto, permanece no cargo por força de uma decisão liminar .

Segundo o MPRJ, há indícios de vínculos do grupo criminoso com Professor Lucas e seu assessor especial, Ronaldo Vieira Cinquine .

A investigação identificou registros de movimentações financeiras, incluindo um pagamento de R$ 20 mil destinado a uma empresa de consultoria e outro de R$ 3 mil diretamente ao assessor.

De acordo com o MPRJ, a organização criminosa teria usado a proximidade com integrantes da administração municipal para obter vantagens ilícitas e ampliar sua influência econômica em Seropédica.

O material também revelou contatos entre o policial e Cinquine.

Milícia já tentava ocupar cargos em prefeituras

Tandera seu fuzil na reunião com os pré-candidatos: 'Se incomodam?' — Foto: Reprodução

A tentativa da milícia de Tandera de interferir em administrações municipais da Baixada Fluminense já havia sido revelada em investigações anteriores .

Em maio de 2023, o g1 mostrou que o miliciano se reuniu com pré-candidatos a prefeituras da região durante a campanha eleitoral de 2020 e ofereceu apoio político em troca de cargos públicos e contratos com as administrações municipais.

As investigações do Gaeco e da 48ª DP (Seropédica) identificaram uma reunião realizada em abril de 2020, na qual Tandera apresentou seus planos para ampliar a influência da organização criminosa sobre o poder público.

“A gente tem que ter o direito a uma licitação . A gente tem que ter o direito a alguma secretaria . Tá me entendendo? Aí as coisas andam, aí a gente faz um elo ”, afirmou Tandera, segundo gravações obtidas na investigação e divulgadas pelo g1 em 2023 .

Em outros trechos, o criminoso explicou que pretendia disputar contratos de menor valor , para evitar chamar a atenção das autoridades .

“Quero coisa pequena, que não vai trazer problema. A empresa que fornece copo, que faz camisa pra prefeitura”, disse o miliciano em um dos trechos da reunião.

Tandera também afirmou que pretendia colocar pessoas de sua confiança à frente de secretarias municipais.

“Secretaria já é outro parâmetro, outras pessoas, já não sou eu. Mas não quer dizer que sai da minha mão. Tenho pessoas capacitadas para gerir as situações”, declarou.

Entre os participantes daquele encontro estavam Luciano Henrique Pereira , conhecido como Luciano da Rede Construir , que disputou a Prefeitura de Seropédica; Thaianna Cristina Barbosa dos Santos , a Doutora Thay , candidata à Prefeitura de Mesquita; e Cornélio Ribeiro , que pretendia concorrer à Prefeitura de Nova Iguaçu, mas desistiu da disputa.

Eles foram denunciados pelo Ministério Público em 2023 por negociar apoio político com a milícia. Luciano e Thaianna concorreram às eleições de 2020, mas não foram eleitos .

O juiz Richard Robert Fairclough , da 1ª Vara Criminal Especializada da Capital, aceitou a denúncia e tornou Luciano, Thay e Cornélio réus por organização criminosa e outros crimes.

Na época, a promotora Glaucia Mello, do Gaeco, afirmou que as investigações haviam identificado uma tentativa de infiltração da milícia na estrutura administrativa dos municípios.

“Nós identificamos relacionamentos dessa organização com a política, uma tentativa de obter secretarias, cargos públicos, contratos administrativos por meio de licitações fraudulentas, o que revela o quão complexa se tornou essa organização criminosa”, declarou.

Tandera e seus disfarces — Foto: Reprodução

Danilo Dias Lima, conhecido como Tandera , é apontado pelas autoridades como chefe de uma milícia que atua principalmente em Seropédica e Nova Iguaçu, na Baixada Fluminense. Ele está foragido da Justiça desde 2016.

Até 2020, Tandera integrava a milícia comandada por Wellington da Silva Braga, o Ecko, mas rompeu com o grupo e passou a disputar territórios com antigos aliados.

Após a morte de Ecko, em uma operação policial em junho de 2021 , Tandera tentou expandir seu domínio para áreas de Santa Cruz e Paciência, na Zona Oeste do Rio, entrando em conflito com a organização liderada por Luis Antônio da Silva Braga, o Zinho, irmão de Ecko.

Segundo investigações divulgadas pelo MPRJ em 2023, a organização criminosa de Tandera atua em atividades como extorsões, homicídios, ameaças, grilagem de terras, exploração ilegal de areais, agiotagem e lavagem de dinheiro.

articles.title: Conheça a Terra Indígena do cacique Raoni, que teve posse reconhecida | G1
articles.standfirst: Território de 362 mil hectares abriga lugares sagrados, cemitérios e a história de uma das principais lideranças indígenas do país.
articles.summary: Território de 362 mil hectares abriga lugares sagrados, cemitérios e a história de uma das principais lideranças indígenas do país.
articles.body:
A Terra Indígena Kapôt Nhĩnore é um território tradicional dos povos Mebêngôkre (Kaiapó) e Yudjá, com aproximadamente 362 mil hectares , localizado entre Mato Grosso e Pará. A área fica em uma região de transição entre os biomas Cerrado e Amazônia e teve a posse reconhecida pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) nesta terça-feira (24).

📑Até o registro final, ainda faltam: a demarcação física, a retirada dos não indígenas, a homologação presidencial e, por fim, a incorporação ao patrimônio da União. Não há prazo para conclusão.

O território também tem importância histórica para o movimento indígena brasileiro. Foi na região que nasceu e cresceu o cacique Raoni Metuktire, uma das principais lideranças indígenas do país e reconhecido internacionalmente pela defesa dos direitos dos povos originários e da preservação ambiental. Atualmente, o líder está em cuidados paliativos devido a um câncer com metástase .

Kapôt Nhĩnore significa "Ponta do Cerrado" na língua Kayapó e faz referência à região de transição entre a Floresta Amazônica e o Cerrado.

Conforme a Fundação dos Povos Indigenas (Funai) há registros da presença Mẽbêngôkre na margem direita do Rio Xingu desde meados do século XIX . A ocupação da região, no entanto, teria começado algumas décadas antes, a partir de deslocamentos vindos das áreas dos rios Araguaia e Tocantins.

O território foi cenário de grandes caçadas , feitos de guerra , cerimônias de nominação e da própria formação do subgrupo Mẽtyktire . A região também abriga cemitérios e lugares considerados sagrados pelos povos indígenas, o que reforça a ligação histórica, cultural e espiritual com o local.

A partir da década de 1930, políticas de ocupação territorial, como a Marcha para o Oeste, e a abertura de rodovias, entre elas as BR-163 e BR-158, contribuíram para intensificar a presença de não indígenas na região. Segundo os registros históricos, o governo de Mato Grosso também vendeu terras públicas sem critérios adequados, ampliando a pressão sobre o território tradicional.

Ainda conforme a Funai, na década de 1950, os irmãos Villas-Bôas convenceram os Mẽtyktire, que haviam sido contatados pouco antes, a se deslocar para áreas ao sul e a oeste do território. A justificativa apresentada era facilitar o acesso a mercadorias e serviços de saúde. O período seguinte, porém, foi marcado por epidemias graves entre os indígenas.

Parte importante de Kapôt Nhĩnore ficou de fora do anteprojeto do Parque Indígena do Xingu, elaborado em 1952. A exclusão abriu caminho para novas remoções e para o avanço da ocupação não indígena na região, em meio a conflitos fundiários e problemas humanitários.

território tradicional dos povos Mebêngôkre (Kaiapó) e Yudjá — Foto: Instituto Raoni

Segundo o Instituto de Pesquisa Ambiental da Amazônia (Ipam), a Terra Indígena Kapôt Nhĩnore está localizada no chamado Arco do Desmatamento , na porção sul do bioma Amazônia e ao norte do Cerrado.

A área está entre remanescentes florestais e uma fronteira agrícola em expansão. O avanço das pastagens e das lavouras, além da presença de atividades ilegais, como garimpo e grilagem de terras, aumenta a pressão sobre o território.

Dados apresentados pela Funai e divulgados pelo governo federal apontam que o desmatamento na região passou de 4.178 hectares, em 2000, para 58 mil hectares em 2026.

A região foi onde nasceu e cresceu o líder indígena Raoni — Foto: Instituo Raoni

Em 2012, a Justiça Federal condenou a União pela demora na demarcação e regularização da área, após uma ação movida pelo Ministério Público Federal (MPF). Em 2015, a Funai instaurou um Grupo Técnico responsável pelos estudos antropológicos e pelos demais levantamentos necessários à identificação e delimitação do território.

O processo de demarcação de terras indígenas prevê sete etapas. A identificação e delimitação da área, primeira fase, foi concluída pela Funai em 2003. Já a publicação da portaria declaratória, que reconhece os limites do território, corresponde à terceira etapa do procedimento.

A medida foi publicada após uma visita do presidente Lula à região, no dia 19 de novembro, quando ele se encontrou com o cacique Raoni.

Apesar do avanço, o processo ainda precisa passar por outras etapas: a demarcação física do território, a retirada de ocupantes não indígenas, a homologação pelo presidente da República e, por fim, o registro da terra em nome da União. Não há prazo definido para a conclusão de todas as fases.

Com o reconhecimento da posse avança o processo para a demarcação da área — Foto: Instituto Raoni

articles.title: Natal em Barra Mansa: Justiça suspende contrato de R$ 8,6 milhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão foi tomada após ação civil pública do Ministério Público do Estado do Rio de Janeiro. Em caso de descumprimento, multa diária será de R$ 50 mil.
articles.summary: Decisão foi tomada após ação civil pública do Ministério Público do Estado do Rio de Janeiro. Em caso de descumprimento, multa diária será de R$ 50 mil.
articles.body:
Justiça suspende contrato de R$ 8,6 milhões para decoração de Natal em Barra Mansa. — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Barra Mansa

A Justiça suspendeu, na segunda-feira (23), a execução de um contrato de aproximadamente R$ 8,6 milhões destinado à decoração de Natal em Barra Mansa (RJ). A decisão foi tomada após uma ação civil pública do Ministério Público do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (MPRJ).

Segundo o MPRJ, a investigação foi iniciada após o recebimento de uma notícia de fato sobre os elevados gastos previstos pela prefeitura com a contratação de serviços de ornamentação, iluminação e cenografia para o Natal de 2026, em meio a dificuldades financeiras e problemas na prestação de serviços públicos essenciais.

De acordo com a Promotoria, a administração municipal vinha alegando, reiteradamente, insuficiência de recursos financeiros para solucionar problemas em áreas prioritárias, como saúde, educação, assistência social e atendimento a mulheres em situação de violência doméstica e familiar.

Ainda segundo o Ministério Público, em fevereiro deste ano, a Prefeitura de Barra Mansa decretou calamidade pública financeira na área da assistência social.

Na decisão, a desembargadora relatora da 1ª Câmara de Direito Público determinou:

A devolução aos cofres públicos de eventuais valores já pagos;

A proibição de novas contratações diretas ou por modalidades excepcionais de dispensa de licitação para a mesma finalidade;

O pagamento de multa diária de R$ 50 mil em caso de descumprimento da decisão judicial.

O g1 procurou a assessoria da Prefeitura de Barra Mansa, que não respondeu até a publicação desta reportagem.

articles.title: Robótica 2026: João Pessoa sedia maior evento da América Latina | G1
articles.standfirst: Cerimônia de abertura acontece nesta terça-feira (24), no Teatro Pedra do Reino. Evento terá três competições valendo vagas para campeonato mundial de robótica.
articles.summary: O Robótica 2026 começa nesta terça (24) no Centro de Convenções com competições de inteligência artificial e entrada gratuita para o público em João Pessoa.
articles.body:
Etapa regional Paraíba da Olimpíada Brasileira de Robótica acontece em João Pessoa — Foto: Dayse Euzébio/Secom-JP

O Robótica 2026, maior evento de robótica e inteligência artificial da América Latina, começa nesta terça-feira (24), em João Pessoa . A programação acontece no Centro de Convenções da capital paraibana até 29 de novembro e reúne mais de 2 mil pesquisadores e estudantes da área.

A cerimônia de abertura será realizada nesta terça-feira (24), às 14h, no Teatro Pedra do Reino.

O evento terá entrada gratuita para o público. Ao longo da programação, serão realizadas três competições: a Mostra Nacional de Robótica, a Competição Brasileira de Robótica e a Olimpíada Brasileira de Robótica.

As competições ocorrerão em um formato híbrido, com disputas presenciais e à distância, para a acessibilidade de equipes brasileiras e internacionais. Durante os dias, também acontecerão congressos e workshops para os participantes.

Os vencedores das competições poderão disputar vagas para a RoboCup 2027, na Alemanha.

João Pessoa recebe evento pela segunda vez

Esta é a segunda vez que João Pessoa recebe o Robótica. A primeira foi em 2018, quando mais de 1.500 competidores participaram do evento.

Em 2014, a capital paraibana também recebeu a RoboCup, uma das principais competições de robótica do mundo.

articles.title: Homem corre com corpo em chamas após colisão entre motos no PA | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente, que ocorreu no centro de Tucuruí, nesta segunda-feira, 23.
articles.summary: Um grave acidente em Tucuruí deixou três feridos nesta segunda-feira (23); imagens mostram uma das vítimas com o corpo em chamas após a colisão entre duas motos.
articles.body:
Um acidente entre duas motocicletas deixou três pessoas feridas nesta segunda-feira (23), na avenida 7 de Setembro, na região central de Tucuruí , no sudeste do Pará.

Uma das motos pegou fogo após a colisão, e um dos ocupantes ficou com o corpo coberto pelas chamas. Ele foi internado na sala vermelha de um hospital da região e deve ser transferido para Belém. O estado de saúde das outras vítimas não foi divulgado.

O acidente ocorreu por volta das 13h07 e foi registrado por uma câmera de segurança. As imagens mostram as duas motocicletas trafegando no mesmo sentido da via.

Em determinado momento, os veículos se encostam, os condutores perdem o controle e as motos derrapam na pista.

Logo após a queda, uma das motocicletas pega fogo. Um dos motociclistas aparece correndo com as roupas em chamas, enquanto pessoas que estavam nas proximidades tentam ajudá-lo a apagar o fogo.

Na sequência, uma mulher aparece com um extintor de incêndio e consegue apagar as chamas que atingiram a pista.

Equipes do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foram acionadas e prestaram os primeiros atendimentos às vítimas. Os feridos foram encaminhados para atendimento médico. O estado de saúde deles não foi divulgado.

articles.title: Mexico to try ‘El Chapo Isidro’ despite US extradition request
articles.summary: Fausto Meza Flores faces drug trafficking and weapons charges after his capture in a violent Sinaloa operation.
articles.body:
Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, an alleged cartel leader known as “El Chapo Isidro”, will be tried in Mexico despite an extradition request by the US, in a move that could worsen already-strained relations between the two countries.

Attorney General Ernestina Godoy told reporters on Monday that Mexican authorities “are going to put him on trial in this country”.

Meza Flores , one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives, was captured after an hours-long firefight between Mexican forces and cartel gunmen on Friday at a compound in Guasave, in the northwestern state of Sinaloa. He was flown to Mexico City the following day.

He faces local charges for weapons offences and methamphetamine possession with intent to sell.

Earlier on Monday, Security Minister Omar Garcia Harfuch said Washington had requested Meza Flores’s extradition after his capture in the northern state of Sinaloa.

President Claudia Sheinbaum said US authorities provided intelligence support but did not participate directly on the ground.

US surveillance drones were authorised to help track Meza Flores before ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠the raid, authorities added, despite sensitivities over US anti-drug operations in the country in recent months.

Four Mexican soldiers and 16 alleged cartel gunmen were killed in the overnight operation, according to the Mexican Secretariat of National Defence.

Meza Flores is accused by US authorities of leading a major trafficking network that moved heroin, cocaine, methamphetamine, marijuana and fentanyl across the border.

The US Department of Justice said he faces six charges in the US that include running a continuing criminal enterprise, narcoterrorism, money laundering conspiracy and weapons offences.

His arrest is the latest in a series of high-profile anti-cartel operations by Mexico, including the February killing of Nemesio “El Mencho” Oseguera, as US President Donald ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Trump presses ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌the Sheinbaum government to crack down on organised crime.

articles.title: WHO chief visits Cuba as healthcare system deteriorates
articles.summary: Analysts say fuel shortages blamed on US sanctions are worsening the crisis.
articles.body:
The World Health Organization’s top official is in Cuba, as the island continues to suffer under an ailing healthcare system amid an economic crisis deepened by United States sanctions.

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus visited a paediatric cardiology centre in Havana on Monday alongside the country’s Public Health Minister Dr Jose Angel Portal Miranda.

“Hola, Havana!” Tedros wrote in a post on X during his tour. “Here for a visit to discuss Cuba’s health situation, challenged by sanctions, fuel and electricity shortages.”

The WHO leader arrived Sunday at the invitation of health authorities in the Caribbean nation for a three-day visit, the second time he has visited Cuba as WHO director-general.

Portal Miranda welcomed Tedros, saying it was an opportunity for him to see firsthand the reality of the Cuban healthcare system and the challenges that it faces.

Cuba’s once-vaunted system of free universal healthcare has deteriorated sharply.

Analysts say the crisis has been compounded by fuel shortages that they blame on stricter US sanctions on the island’s energy sector , worsening an economy that already had been limping for years.

A government report released in June said that the survival rate for children with cancer had fallen to 65 percent from 85 percent, before the energy blockade began in January.

Hospitals across Cuba face shortages of supplies including syringes, gauze, vaccines and anaesthetics. They also lack spare parts to repair equipment such as haemodialysis and CT scan machines.

“The situation is shocking,” said Mario Cruz Penate, the Pan American Health Organization and WHO representative on the island.

He noted that Cuba has long enjoyed health indicators comparable to those of developed nations, including low mortality, high life expectancy, broad vaccination coverage and widespread prenatal care.

articles.title: Pope Francis battled visions of the devil during a two-year spiritual crisis, diaries reveal
articles.summary: Pope Francis suffered a spiritual crisis during his papacy in which he saw visions of the devil and hell while struggling with how to exercise power, newly published diaries of the late pontiff reveal.
articles.body: Pope Francis suffered a spiritual crisis during his papacy in which he saw visions of the devil and hell while struggling with how to exercise power, newly published diaries of the late pontiff reveal. The Argentine pope intermittently kept a diary between 1992 and 2024, first during his time as a bishop in Argentina and then following his election as pope. Now, several of those entries have been compiled in a book published on Tuesday. It was written by Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández, one of Francis’ closest aides and a fellow Argentine, who offers a detailed commentary on the papal diaries. The 160-page “The Private Diary of Pope Francis” is focused primarily on the pope’s spiritual life and pastoral agenda, although it also details how the first Latin American pope struggled with temptations connected to the use of power in 2021-2022. It also includes what the pope describes as encounters with the devil along with his thoughts about his successor, Leo XIV, whom he described as “irreproachable.” The publication of papal diaries is rare, but not unprecedented, and can provide unusually personal insights. While some popes order that their personal papers be destroyed, the diaries of John XXIII were published posthumously, as were some papers of John Paul II. Francis wrote 86 pages of the black-covered diary — initially a planner for the year 1992 — while he was in Argentina and 55 pages while he was pope. “He showed me a few books, including what looked like an old agenda book with a leather cover. When he opened it, I saw that it was filled with notes in his handwriting. He told me, ‘From this, you will all see,’” Fernández wrote. Here are some of the major revelations: Encounters with the devil and the entrance to hell The diaries say that the pope experienced “frequent demonic attacks,” and Francis details three encounters with the devil: two while he was archbishop of Buenos Aires and another in 2018, when he was pope. Francis wrote that the devil has “eyes of fire,” also describing them as “menacing” and “seductive” eyes. “I can’t forget his eyes the first two times — from the car when I was returning to the house, and in the choir loft during Mass. However, he always reappears in different situations,” the pope wrote in an entry for August 18, 2024. The third occasion came after returning from a visit to Chile in 2018, a trip overshadowed by the clerical sexual abuse scandal. “On one occasion, a few days after returning to Rome, I was in a meeting. I saw him and heard his voice [his underlining], triumphant, possessing everything: ‘Now I’ve gotten everything I wanted,’” the pope wrote on January 24, 2021. “Just as I can’t forget his eyes from the previous two, in this case, I can’t forget the powerful raspiness of his voice. The Lord granted me an opportunity to leave that meeting, and he thus freed me.” Catholic teaching holds that the devil is a fallen angel and a real presence, and Catholic tradition cautions that those who are serious about attaining holiness will often encounter strong spiritual opposition. During his pontificate, Francis would frequently mention the devil, linking it to gossip and money. “The devil enters through the pockets,” he often said. The diary also includes details of how Francis believed God spoke to him in dreams. On one occasion, Francis recounted seeing “the entrance to hell.” The pope, in 2018, described it as a form of “pagan seduction in full force,” an apparent reference to the worshipping of idols. “I peeked in to look a little and it terrified me. It was before going to sleep. I grabbed the rosary as a weapon. I thank the Lord for this help,” he wrote. A spiritual crisis The book reveals that in 2021-2022, Francis underwent a spiritual crisis connected to a temptation or “curiosity” with power and which was partly connected to excessive activity and feelings of self-sufficiency. It was, the pope explained, also linked to “governance issues, pressure regarding decisions to make, and aridity and desolation.” To counter the temptation, he sought to exercise greater humility and patience, even leaving people in place in the church’s central administration who others felt were undermining his papacy. During his 12-year pontificate, Francis, initiated several reforms in the church, including on the treatment of LGBTQ Catholics and the role of women, but faced significant opposition. Some of it came from inside the Vatican, where some bishops and cardinals openly resisted his reforms. “One time in my presence, a bishop asked him why he had not yet fired someone in the Roman Curia who had been speaking badly of him in public and pursuing a personal agenda very different than his,” wrote Cardinal Fernández, who was appointed by Francis to lead the Vatican’s doctrine office. “After an interminable silence, he responded by explaining that he felt a strong sensation in his heart that God did not want him to become a puppeteer who uses and manipulates people according to his own convenience. He explained that, for this reason, he preferred to let that person remain in his position.” While the diary doesn’t go into specific examples, the pope wrote on December 30, 2022, that he refused the temptation to treat “others like puppets.” In 2018, he said that “this sense of self-sufficiency and I can solve everything brought me to the gates of hell. I can’t forget the day I saw it.” The crisis that Francis underwent, Fernández explained, was “connected to power” and the curiosity to “discover what it is like to exercise one’s own power.” As a member of the Jesuit religious order, the pope was continuously engaged in a spiritual discernment, essentially engaging in self-examination to determine whether he was working for self-interest or the good of others. For Francis, feeling that he was “above the world” through his power was “the path of the worst spiritual worldliness imaginable, which he sought to dismantle by avoiding every symbol or expression of papal ‘majesty’ or ‘glory,’” Fernández added. During his pontificate, Francis adopted a simple style, living in a Vatican guesthouse, wearing black orthopedic shoes and refusing certain papal vestments. Abuse crisis, exhaustion and his successor While the diaries focus on the pope’s spiritual life, they do include comments about the clerical sexual abuse crisis, including in Chile in 2018. At the time, Francis was criticized for dismissing the case of a bishop who had been accused of witnessing and covering up abuse when he was a priest. The pope later apologized for his handling of the case and summoned all the bishops from the country to Rome. In an unprecedented move, the bishops offered their resignations to the pope en masse. “Devastated because of the situation in Chile and the dialogue with the journalists on the airplane. I fell off the cot then,” Francis wrote. “It was hard for me to admit what happened in Chile; I didn’t think it was so serious.” The phrase “fell off the cot,” the book explains, means to suddenly wake up to something. Francis would go on to make several reforms aimed at tackling clerical sexual abuse. The diaries reveal the pope’s thoughts on Cardinal Robert Prevost, the future Pope Leo XIV, whom Francis brought to the Vatican to lead the department for appointing bishops. According to Fernández, Francis called Prevost “a great pastor, a generous missionary, and an irreproachable man.” He was also generous to his critics, including Cardinals Robert Sarah, a Guinean, and Gerhard Muller, a German prelate. The Argentine pontiff said Sarah had “a refined spiritual sensitivity” and that Muller “seems aggressive but he’s a good man,” Fernández wrote. The diaries reveal Pope Francis’ dedication to his ministry, frequently mentioning feelings of exhaustion, both in Argentina and after his election. Francis rarely took a day off and never went on vacation outside the Vatican. In 2019, he described himself as “feeling exhausted, almost without spiritual support and without a point of reference.” The diaries, Cardinal Fernández explained, aim to show the heart of Jorge Mario Bergoglio, who was elected pope and took the name Francis on March 13, 2013. They show someone who was hard on himself but demanded the same dedication from all priests. Francis died on Easter Monday, April 21, 2025, at the age of 88 after having been hospitalized with double pneumonia in the weeks previously. During the final days of his life, he defied doctor’s orders to greet people in St. Peter’s Square. “His total dedication, coupled with frequently feeling completely exhausted, speaks of heroism in pastoral charity,” Fernández said. The pope’s funeral, on April 26, 2025, in a packed St. Peter’s Square, was attended by thousands, including heads of state from across the world. Francis’ diaries are being published by the Vatican Publishing house. Image Books, an imprint of Penguin Random House Christian Publishing Group, is releasing the English-language version in the United States and Canada.

articles.title: Unsigned acts 'live dream' at Peter Gabriel's Real World Studios
articles.summary: Seven unsigned West Country acts record at Peter Gabriel's famous studio.
articles.body:
For most aspiring musicians, spending four days recording in a world-famous studio would be out of reach.

But seven unsigned acts from across the West Country have been given that opportunity after being selected from more than 400 applicants to record at Peter Gabriel's renowned Real World Studios in Wiltshire.

The artists will follow in the footsteps of acts including Harry Styles, Coldplay and Amy Winehouse after being chosen by a panel of industry experts as part of a scheme funded through a partnership between Real World and Arts Council England.

"It's a huge privilege," said Luca Williamson, drummer with Bristol band 1000 Legs. "These places are so hard to access."

For many of the musicians, it is their first time recording in a professional studio.

By the end of the programme, each act will leave with a fully mixed and mastered EP.

The opportunity comes at a time when many emerging artists are balancing music with work, study and rising living costs.

"Most of us are students, working hospitality jobs at the same time as well as trying to pay the rent," said saxophonist Gabriel Bonner-Thomas, of 1000 Legs.

"It's hard on time and money, so you have to be so passionate about it. Over the course of a month it could be £60 each just to rehearse, there aren't a lot of spaces to do it, it's tough."

The chance to record at Real World would normally be beyond the reach of many unsigned musicians.

"The list of people who've recorded here is really cool, but it's also being in a room which is this acoustically brilliant, with this much amazing gear, and recording to tape is something we'd never be able to afford," said guitarist Jerome Gamlin.

Bassist Ben Lefever added: "It is very different, because a lot of the time when you practice you are so focused on your own instrument, but when you get in here, such a high-class studio, you get to hear everything played back at you in the way it's intended to be heard."

Guitarist Cass Dener said opportunities like this could make a significant difference to artists outside major music hubs.

"So much talent goes unnoticed because of location, people who live in small towns without venues, so for Real World to give this opportunity is a lovely thing," he said.

Another artist who has been chosen to record at Real World Studios - singing in the same space as Beyoncé, Björk and Alicia Keys - is Bristol vocalist Aloka Collister.

"It took me a whole day to accept I'm actually doing this," said the 23-year-old.

"It feels cosmic, this thing I could only have ever dreamed of is happening in my reality, I'm very emotional," she added.

Collister said music had helped her through difficult periods in her life.

"I struggle with depression, I struggle to leave the house sometimes," she said.

"Singing is baring your heart and soul, sometimes I've been on stage in a vulnerable state. Music makes me feel free.

"Now I've got to do something like this, maybe I can try to sort out those things," she added.

For staff at Real World, opening the doors to grassroots musicians has been one of the most rewarding parts of the project.

"I think it can be a life-changing thing, learning that a space like this is also for them, not just for others," said head engineer Katie May.

"You get to see them walk in and their reaction, it's our job to make them feel as comfortable as they can.

"Aloka is an incredible vocalist, one of the best I've ever worked with."

Amanda Jones, label manager at Real World Records, said the scheme was designed to help talented artists access opportunities that are becoming harder to find.

"We wanted to make sure new artists from the south west could come through the door and use these amazing facilities.

"It is such a challenge in the industry today to make a living as a professional musician, but some of these young people are so gloriously talented you just want to give them every opportunity you can."

The initiative comes against a backdrop of growing pressures on musicians.

According to the Musicians' Union, average annual earnings remained at £20,000 between 2013 and 2023, failing to keep pace with inflation and rising living costs.

"It's got much harder for emerging artists." said the union's general secretary, Naomi Pohl.

"The cost of touring has gone up, Brexit has made it more difficult to earn a living in Europe, there are fewer opportunities and it's more difficult to earn a living."

"That's why schemes like this from Peter Gabriel are so important for musicians, to give them a foothold.

"The problem is that the scheme has been massively oversubscribed, only a handful of musicians can be chosen from hundreds, that's a tough situation," she said

The seven selected west country music acts will be invited back to Real World Studios in February 2027, to perform to a panel of industry experts.

articles.title: Ellesmere residents oppose plan for seven new houses
articles.summary: A planning application has been put in to build homes next to the town's cemetery and large mere.
articles.body:
People living next to one of Shropshire's best-known natural tourist attractions have said plans to build houses there would be "devastating" to its ecosystem.

A planning application has been put in to build seven houses on land off Swan Hill, in Ellesmere, next to the town's cemetery and large mere.

Campaigner and conservationist Rob McBride said he believed a greenfield site was being "sacrificed" and the houses would ruin the land.

In submitted documents, the land agent's Berrys said that "no essential features of the conservation area or other significant heritage features would be harmed by the proposed development."

It added that "appropriate timing of works and subsequent enhancement of the remaining scrub will ensure not only a gain in habitat units, but a gain in biodiversity value".

"No evidence of protected species was found on or around the site, and potential to support such species was considered."

McBride, who has been a conservationist for more than two decades, said he thought important features of the site were not mentioned in the plan's ecological survey, and that key species were present.

"We are lucky that we have a chartered ecologist who lives in one of the houses here so she has put her objection in," he added.

The chair of the local Heronwatch Group Edward Bevan added there was "amphibian migration" across where the houses could be built.

"For many years, people have been watching toads and newts crossing on their annual migration, crossing the road very near the development and they are of course protected species," he said.

"Anything that harms their route through the area in order to do their migration down to the mere for breeding, anything that harms that is detrimental."

Former park ranger Wendy Salter, a regular volunteer who has helped maintain the beauty spot, said more "social housing or housing that young people can afford is needed".

"South of the town, the town council have got land allocated [for houses], we've got building sites happening in the town at the moment, the town has grown and is continuing to grow.

"My issue isn't with that, it's seven houses - [it] sounds like nothing but it's the sharp end of the wedge and those houses will go for a lot of money because the view's over the mere."

In planning documents, Berrys said "the evidence base behind the draft Local Plan also indicates that Ellesmere is within a 10% affordable housing target rate area."

It added: "A minimum of 10% of all the units provided on the site would therefore be affordable units, which on a seven dwelling development equals 0.7. This equates to a financial contribution of £63,000."

The money contributed by the developer would be donated to Shropshire Council to build an affordable home elsewhere.

After a public planning meeting last week, Ellesmere Town Council unanimously voted to oppose the plans.

The town's mayor Pete Jones said the authority had listened to feedback, the size of which was bigger than "any other application" in his time in local politics.

"Everybody who spoke at the meeting had a different valid material reason to object to this application. I think we counted over 22 different reasons just raised at that meeting by different people," he added.

"We would typically see less than 10 comments pro or against an application so to see over 200 is really extraordinary."

In a statement, Shropshire Council said: "This planning application will be considered in the usual way through the council's planning process.

"The council has an established scheme of delegation which sets out whether planning applications are determined by officers or by the relevant planning committee. Applications are considered in accordance with those arrangements.

"In addition, the council is required to follow the government's prescribed scheme of delegation and assessment process when determining planning applications.

"All relevant planning matters and representations received will be taken into account before a decision is made, and it would not be appropriate to comment further while the application is under consideration."

articles.title: Bengaluru man gets Rs 4 ‘location surcharge’ on medicines, fights MedPlus in consumer court, pharmacy ordered to pay Rs 5,000 compensation and Rs 2,000 costs
articles.summary: BENGALURU: It was only Rs 4, but a 36-year-old Sarjapura resident refused to let it go.
articles.body: BENGALURU: It was only Rs 4, but a 36-year-old Sarjapura resident refused to let it go. Charged a "location surcharge" on top of the printed price of his medicines, he fought it for months, first by email and then in the consumer court. The Bangalore (Urban) District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has now held pharmacy chain MedPlus guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.The dispute began on September 25, 2025, when the complainant bought medicines from the MedPlus Pharmacy outlet in Sarjapura for Rs 1,113. The invoice carried an extra line, "Location Surcharge Fees", of Rs 4, inclusive of GST, even though medicines are sold at the maximum retail price (MRP).He emailed the company the same day and sent follow-ups and reminders until October 3, asking for a refund and for the practice to stop. The company's reply, the commission noted, was that "ongoing maintenance costs" across its locations had forced it to introduce a small surcharge to help maintain its shops. He received no refund, only a reply citing maintenance costs.On January 19, 2026, he approached the commission, appearing in person. He sought a refund of Rs 4, Rs 1 lakh for mental agony and harassment, and Rs 10,000 for litigation and incidental costs. Optival Health Solutions Pvt. Ltd., which operates MedPlus, and its Sarjapura branch did not appear despite notice, nor did they file a reply. The commission placed them ex parte.Relying on a National Commission ruling, Kotak Mahindra Old Mutual vs Dr Nishi Gupta, the commission held that not filing a written version amounts to admission of the complaint's allegations. It added that the company's own email replies admitted the surcharge was being collected, and that the invoice showed it plainly.The commission rejected the maintenance argument. It said the MRP already covers taxes, retailer margin, transport and maintenance, and that shop upkeep is a business overhead to be met from the retailer's profit margin. It cannot be passed on to customers as a fee without prior disclosure and consent. It noted that charging above MRP is an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and that the Legal Metrology rules and the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013, bar the sale of medicines above the printed MRP. Consumer fora, it said, have consistently held that no retailer can charge even a rupee over MRP under labels such as handling or convenience fees.The commission, comprising president Ramachandra M S and members Nandini H Kumbhar and Savitha Airani, on October 30 allowed the complaint in part. articles.title: China sentences official to death for passing state secrets to foreign spy
articles.summary: China has sentenced a government official to death for handing over state secrets and classified documents to a foreign intelligence agent.
articles.body: China has sentenced a government official to death for handing over state secrets and classified documents to a foreign intelligence agent. In a public post, Monday, China’s National Administration of State Secrets Protection said the convicted official was approached and recruited by a foreign woman while working overseas. It is extremely rare for China to disclose that it has sentenced someone to death for espionage, or publish details on proceedings involving national security. The post did not mention where the official was posted, but gave his surname as Ma, and said he had been approached by a woman named ‘Kailin,’ who initially said she was interested to learn Chinese. It did not say what the woman’s nationality was. After their relationship developed, ‘Kailin’ began shifting their chats to “politically sensitive” topics and major international developments, and convinced Ma to hand over sensitive information about the personnel and operations of a Chinese institution in the country, according to prosecutors. Kailin later introduced Ma to her other colleagues and told him that if he did not become an agent for their country, they would tip off the Chinese government about his activities. Ma then signed a pledge of loyalty, starting down the path “being consumed by darkness, and doomed beyond redemption,” the statement said. The official later returned to China and sent “hundreds” of classified intelligence documents to the foreign agent in return for a fixed monthly income with additional bonus when he provided key material, according to the statement. China’s prosecutor found Ma sent nine documents classified as state secrets and 26 documents classified as confidential in return for more than $150,000 for the espionage activities. The state secrets administration’s post offered a stern warning to Chinese citizens to “maintain vigilance in our social and personal lives, adhere strictly to workplace discipline, and guard against being targeted, manipulated or exploited by hostile actors.” The verdict comes as China steps up its anti-espionage efforts as its strategic rivalry with the US-led west deepens. In 2023 China broadened the scope of its already sweeping counter-espionage law to expand the definition of espionage from covering state secrets and intelligence to any “documents, data, materials or items related to national security and interests,” without specifying specific parameters for how these terms are defined. Earlier this year its spy agency warned that China’s young people were being duped by foreign forces into shirking hard work and prioritizing their individual emotions at the expense of national development. The post from the State Security Ministry’s official account warned young people to stay vigilant against “complex opinion traps” and any “lying flat” narratives that propagate the message that hard work is futile.

articles.title: Pakistan’s Zeeshan Ali set for historic flight to China’s space station
articles.summary: The Pakistan Air Force pilot will spend about a week on board the Tiangong, conducting experiments with China’s crew.
articles.body:
Islamabad, Pakistan – Pakistan is poised to send an astronaut into space for the first time on Wednesday, when an air force pilot joins China’s Shenzhou-24 mission to the country’s Tiangong space station.

Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, 40, will fly as a payload specialist alongside commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi. The spacecraft is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China at 8:18am Beijing time (00:18 GMT), or 5:18am in Pakistan.

Speaking at a news conference in Jiuquan on Tuesday, China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) spokesperson Zhang Jingbo said the mission would mark the first joint flight by Chinese and foreign astronauts in the country’s crewed space programme.

After reaching orbit, the spacecraft will carry out a rapid, autonomous rendezvous lasting about three and a half hours before docking with the forward port of the station’s Tianhe core module, Zhang said.

Ali’s stay will be brief. He will return to Earth on board the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft after a short joint flight, while Zhu Yangzhu, a member of that crew, remains in orbit for a year, Zhang said.

Pakistan’s Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO) has said Ali will spend about a week on the station.

“I want to assure you that I am not flying for myself. I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis,” Ali told reporters during the crew’s conversation with the media.

Ali and Khurram Daud, a second Pakistani selected for astronaut training, are Pakistan Air Force pilots.

They were selected through a three-stage process that began with screening in Pakistan and included medical, psychological and technical assessments.

CMSA named them reserve astronauts on April 22 earlier this year. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met them in Islamabad the following day, and on April 24, China’s Space Day, they joined the Astronaut Center of China in Beijing for training.

Before leaving, Daud asked Pakistanis to pray for him in a video released by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

“My message to you all is to pray for me, so that I can complete this training and this mission well, and make my nation and my country proud,” he said in Urdu.

Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, who is in China for the launch, paid tribute to both men on X on Tuesday.

“They trained in centrifuges and simulators, in emergency drills and in a new language. Both performed exceptionally well in training. Though Zeeshan Ali will fly tomorrow both have already made Pakistan proud,” he wrote.

Thanking his instructors, SUPARCO and CMSA, at Tuesday’s news conference, Ali said: “No matter who flies, we have already made the history together.”

Daud was not named in the crew, and it is not yet clear whether he will fly on a later mission.

In written responses to Al Jazeera, SUPARCO said the backup astronauts would serve as experts to help carry the programme forward.

Zhang said Ali would take part in the crew’s daily work but would mainly oversee China-Pakistan experiments, install samples and equipment and conduct tests in orbit.

The mission will include four joint science projects in biotechnology and materials, Zhang said. Ali will also conduct an experiment involving cyanobacteria, photosynthetic microorganisms.

Pakistan’s Information Ministry said in April that the experiments would cover materials science, fluid physics, life sciences and biotechnology, with potential applications in climate resilience, food security and industrial innovation.

Qamarul Islam, a space scientist and former senior official in the state-affiliated Institute of Space Technology (IST) in Islamabad, said the experiments had been shortlisted after SUPARCO invited research institutes in Pakistan to submit proposals.

“Primarily these experiments are the experiments of the research institutes, universities and others, from Pakistan,” he told Al Jazeera.

SUPARCO said the station was a fully equipped laboratory. It added in its response that Ali’s week in orbit was meant to start and install the experiments, and to record data confirming that the equipment had survived launch loads and vibrations and was safely installed in microgravity.

“Completing the four experiments takes between six and 12 months,” it said.

According to Zhang, preparations focused on professional skills, crew coordination and language.

“We focus on Chinese commands and technical terms to ensure accurate execution,” he said, in the English interpretation of his remarks.

In a promotional video by the Chinese space agency, Ali, who described himself as a fighter pilot, said centrifuge, rescue and survival, and emergency procedures training were part of his preparation.

“But the real challenge, honestly speaking, was mastering the Chinese language, because all the switches, all the software, all the programmes, all the voice announcements, everything is in Chinese. So we had to learn that and master that technical Chinese,” he said.

SUPARCO and CMSA signed their astronaut agreement in Islamabad in February 2025. Ali said the two countries had since moved quickly.

“The two great nations of China and Pakistan have turned a pilot into an astronaut in a remarkably short span of time,” he said.

This year marks 75 years of diplomatic ties between the two neighbours. Zhang described the flight as another milestone in their cooperation.

“Pakistan is China’s all-weather strategic cooperative partner,” Zhang said, according to the English interpretation of his remarks.

Pakistan’s Information Ministry said in April that the programme placed the country among a select group of nations involved in human spaceflight.

China built its own space station after being excluded from the International Space Station (ISS), in part because a 2011 US law bars NASA from bilateral cooperation with Beijing.

“Chinese were left out. And obviously China developed their own space station. Pakistan is also out of the International Space Station as far as the astronauts are concerned,” Qamar said.

He said China’s decision to choose Pakistan for its first foreign visitor reflected the two countries’ closeness.

Asked by a reporter on Tuesday whether China would expand cooperation, including joint flights with Russia, Zhang pointed to the station’s transport and astronaut-training systems. He said China hoped to explore space with more countries and regions.

SUPARCO said Pakistan was opening a path for international collaboration on the Chinese station and could now offer its expertise to other countries.

Asked by China’s state-run CGTN about the future of the partnership, Ali looked beyond the current mission.

“I believe what comes after this flight matters more than the flight itself. This mission is not a finish line; it is a launchpad. And I hope the next chapter of China-Pakistan space cooperation to grow from one astronaut, one flight, to multiple joint flights, to Moon, Mars, and beyond.”

Pakistan’s government has also set a lunar target.

Asked about lunar plans, SUPARCO said Pakistan was already working with China on a lunar mission tentatively planned for 2028. It said it could not yet disclose details.

Pakistan’s lunar programme has so far focused on robotic missions. The iCube-Qamar satellite, developed at IST, reached the lunar orbit on board China’s Chang’e-6 mission in 2024. A SUPARCO-developed rover is due to fly on the Chang’e-8 about 2028.

Qamar, who was the project director for iCube-Qamar, said lunar missions ranged from flybys and orbiters, such as the satellite, to landings and eventually permanent bases.

“In the long term you will see stations on the Moon, a utilisation of the Moon,” he said.

China is also advancing its lunar programme. Zhang said preparations were under way for tests of the Long March-10 rocket and Mengzhou crewed spacecraft. The first flight of the Lanyue lunar lander was on track, he said. Beijing aims to put astronauts on the Moon by 2030.

For Pakistan, Qamar said, sending a person into space would introduce scientific challenges beyond the technology of getting there, including coping with isolation and supplying oxygen and food.

“I think it will be really good learning for Pakistan to be involved in such thing because then it has many other applications on ground, applications in the medical field and other aspects,” he said.

articles.title: In 2005, Fats Domino stayed in his New Orleans home as Katrina hit; a photograph later showed the rock ’n’ roll legend being helped off a rescue boat in the flooded Ninth Ward
articles.summary: Explore the incredible story of rock 'n' roll legend Fats Domino, who stayed behind in his New Orleans home during Hurricane Katrina and was later rescued amid the floodwaters of the Ninth Ward.
articles.body: During Hurricane Katrina, which hit New Orleans on August 29, 2005, Fats Domino, one of the greatest rock ‘n’ roll artists, stayed in his house located in the Lower Ninth Ward of New Orleans. He became unreachable as water flooded his area when he was 77 years old. His relatives and manager thought that he was lost until a picture of him from a rescue boat appeared. Born Antoine Domino, he lived in the same neighbourhood where he grew up from the beginning of the 1960s. He was famous for such songs as “Blueberry Hill”, “Ain’t That a Shame” and “Blue Monday”.Domino's longtime agent, Al Embry, called him on the Sunday before the hurricane struck and tried to persuade him to evacuate. Embry told Reuters that Domino insisted he was going to "try to ride out" the storm at home. When the floodwaters came into the area, Embry could no longer get hold of him. Enquiries from officials within the city and the state did not aid in finding him.A newspaper photograph confirmed Domino had survivedKaren Domino White, Domino's daughter, spotted her father in a photo published in The Times-Picayune, the first sign that he had survived. This photo was captured on the night of August 29 and portrayed a man who was helped off a boat by some rescuers. The September 2 Los Angeles Times article says that although the photo suggested he had survived, she still did not know where her father had been taken. The Associated Press later confirmed in a May 2007 report that Domino was rescued by boat from his flooded Ninth Ward home after the storm struck on August 29, 2005. CBS News reported that relatives spent four tense days waiting for news before the rescue-boat photograph gave them the first sign he was safe.Katrina left Domino’s home and music collection damagedDomino was able to make it back to his Ninth Ward residence to assess the damage done. In March 2007, according to the Associated Press, Domino walked around his devastated property as the workers began working on the reconstruction of his home, which had been damaged by the floods. The hurricane also took a heavy toll on his musical belongings. May 20, 2007, Los Angeles Times report, published after his first public performance since Katrina, Domino said he had lost his home, pianos, gold and platinum records and much of the city he loved. Eventually, the musician came back on stage in New Orleans in May 2007.Domino’s story is just one of the many individual accounts that emerged because of Hurricane Katrina. This hurricane destroyed New Orleans, wrecked countless homes and made people all over the city leave their homes to look for refuge elsewhere. The ability of Domino’s to survive the rising waters was crucial because he could come back to the neighbourhood where he spent most of his life and, at the same time, marked the moment of his return to the stage and May 2007. The performer will remain strongly linked to New Orleans, the city where he lived and which influenced his music and career.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Hippo Cove at Cincinnati Zoo reopens after Fiona’s death
articles.summary: The Hippo Cove at the Cincinnati Zoo reopened on Monday with new protective measures following the death of their beloved hippo, Fiona, last week, the zoo said.
articles.body: The Hippo Cove at the Cincinnati Zoo reopened on Monday with new protective measures following the death of their beloved hippo Fiona last week, the zoo said. Fiona, whose premature birth and fight for survival captured hearts nearly a decade ago, died Thursday after swallowing a hat that had been tossed by a visitor and flung into the enclosure by a ceiling fan. The hat got lodged in the middle of her small intestine. Fiona was 9 years old. Hippo Cove had closed after Fiona’s death but the habitat reopened Monday with modifications to “guard against something like this ever happening again,” Cincinnati Zoo Director Dave Jenike said in a news release. “We added a layer of netting above the viewing windows and, out of an abundance of caution, removed all ceiling fans in the area,” Jenike said. The hat Fiona swallowed was tossed by a zoo visitor, and a ceiling fan caught it and flung it into the hippo habitat. “The Cincinnati Zoo has been accredited since 1978 and was last accredited in 2025 after an exhaustive inspection, a standard practice for Zoos seeking or renewing accreditation,” said Dan Ashe, president of the Association of Zoos and Aquariums. “Nothing was of concern for the hippo habitat in the inspection report. It seems like it was a freak event that couldn’t have been foreseen.” The Cincinnati Zoo said it relies on visitors to secure their belongings and to inform zoo staff if they see something that shouldn’t be in an animal habitat. Visitors can see other hippos, including Fiona’s 4-year-old brother, Fritz, in Hippo Cove, according to the zoo. Since her death, Fiona’s fans have covered a hippo statue at the zoo with flowers and notes written in crayon. Others left behind watermelons and pumpkins, some of her favorite treats. “She brought so much love in her lifetime,” said one note.

articles.title: Pacific Coast king tides could break records and flood communities
articles.summary: High tides along the Pacific Coast could break 40-year-old records and flood low-lying coastal communities, complicating travel during Thanksgiving week.
articles.body: SAN FRANCISCO — High tides along the Pacific Coast could break 40-year-old records and flood low-lying coastal communities, complicating travel during Thanksgiving week. In the San Francisco Bay Area, tides could reach 2.6 feet (0.8 meters) above normal Tuesday before peaking Wednesday at 2.8 feet (0.9 meters) above normal, said Dial Hoang, a National Weather Service forecaster. The Bay Area’s highest recorded tide reached 2.9 feet (0.9 meters) above normal in San Francisco on Jan. 27, 1983, he said. San Francisco’s famed Embarcadero waterfront, which flooded during heavy rain last week, is again at risk of flooding. King tides, the highest tides of the year, occur when the gravitational pull of the moon and sun aligns to raise water levels. Their effects this year are being amplified by the ongoing super El Niño, which has warmed the ocean, leading to an increased volume of seawater. The weather service issued a high surf warning in the Bay Area on Wednesday, when breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet (6 to 9 meters) could overpower swimmers and sweep people into the ocean. “Remain out of the water and stay off of jetties, piers, and rocks. Never turn your back to the ocean!” the agency said in a social media post. Heavy rain forecast for Tuesday evening into Wednesday could worsen street flooding. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie, who urged people over the weekend to consider avoiding holiday travel because of an “extremely serious” situation, later said the forecast had improved somewhat. “As you make plans for Thanksgiving, keep the weather in mind. Check conditions before traveling, and avoid unnecessary trips when roads are flooded or winds are strong,” he wrote on social media on Monday. Farther north, in Humboldt County near the Oregon border, the sheriff’s office ordered evacuations in a small coastal community where some buildings flooded on Monday, saying people needed to leave by Tuesday morning. “The tides are expected to be higher by Tuesday, and the southerly winds will have been blowing for 24 hours by then, and so that will push the storm surge even higher,” said Matthew Kidwell, a National Weather Service meteorologist in Humboldt County. Coastal flooding also possible in the Pacific Northwest National Weather Service offices in Portland and Seattle warned of coastal flooding through Friday. The most significant flooding could occur Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day as several weather systems bring strong winds and rising surf coinciding with high tides. Waves can sweep people off rocks or knock them off their feet and pull them into the ocean, the agency warned. Washington State Ferries has canceled several sailings because of high tides. About 300,000 people are expected to use the ferry system over the holiday weekend, and extreme tides could disrupt their trips. Heavy snow in the mountains could slow holiday travel over passes, especially along Interstate 90 east of Seattle. More flooding forecast for Florida In South Florida, king tides are expected to cause coastal flooding from Palm Beach to Miami. Water levels could remain elevated for several hours before and after high tide Wednesday and Thursday mornings. A storm arriving Tuesday night could increase the risk of flooding if it moves over land, the National Weather Service said. Many South Florida communities were just beginning to dry out after slow-moving storms dumped more than 17 inches (43 centimeters) of rain less than a week earlier. The St. Johns River has been above flood stage near Cocoa since Nov. 2. Last week, it broke a record set in 1953. The river is forecast to remain at least 2 feet (0.6 meters) above flood stage, according to the weather service.

articles.title: Russian strike kills two in Ukraine, days after ship attack off Libya
articles.summary: Russian attack on Zaporizhzhia destroyed a house and damaged a five-storey apartment building, Ukrainian officials said.
articles.body:
A Russian air attack on Zaporizhzhia in Ukraine has killed two people and wounded more than 40, including an infant, the day after Kyiv said its drones sank a Russian warship in a Libyan port far from the front lines of the war.

Russia’s dawn raid on the city in southeast Ukraine destroyed a house and damaged a five-storey apartment building, regional officials said on Tuesday.

It came as the two warring sides continued long-range attacks, launching hundreds of drones overnight.

Russia’s Ministry of Defence said air defences intercepted and destroyed 699 Ukrainian drones over seven regions, occupied Crimea and the Black Sea.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 355 drones flew towards the capital overnight and 63 were shot down as they approached.

Reporting from Moscow, Al Jazeera’s Amin Dorghami said it had been a “long time” since Moscow had been targeted with as many drones.

Ukraine’s Air Force said Russia launched 96 drones overnight, with hits at 13 locations and 73 shot down or jammed.

Russia’s Defence Ministry said its forces hit an electricity substation in Pryluky, in Ukraine’s Chernihiv region, which it said powered Ukraine’s military. Russian forces also hit a dry cargo ship southwest of Odesa that the ministry said was carrying military supplies.

“This too could be considered routine, since Russia is enforcing a blockade on Ukraine’s Black Sea ports,” Dorghami said.

Late on Monday, the Polish military said a Russian drone briefly entered Poland’s airspace during an attack on western Ukraine but was not shot down because of the risk to civilians. Deputy Defence Minister Pawel Zalewski said he assumed the incursion was deliberate, coming three days after three Russian cruise missiles crashed in eastern Poland.

Reporting from Kyiv, Al Jazeera’s Abdelaziz Mujahid said the incursion “may also signal that the conflict and these confrontations are widening”.

It follows Ukraine’s attack on the Russian corvette Merkury in the Libyan port of Benghazi on Sunday. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said seven Ukrainian-built naval drones were used in the “completely legitimate operation against enemy ships”.

“The strike in Benghazi has left Russia without one of its newest combat ships,” said Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova, reporting from Moscow. “It was commissioned only three years ago.”

Russia’s UN envoy, Vassily Nebenzia, accused Western countries of backing Ukraine’s recent attacks and said Moscow would keep using military means to ensure its security.

On Monday, debris from Russian drones fell in central Kyiv, close to the president’s office and set a five-storey building on fire. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said five people were injured, including a foreign national.

“All of this is a bit too close for comfort for Ukrainians, especially considering that the presidential palace is just a few hundred metres up the road,” reported Al Jazeera’s Audrey McAlpine from the scene.

Zelenskyy said on Monday evening that Ukrainian intelligence warned that Russia was preparing a new series of strikes and urged residents to heed air raid alerts.

articles.title: Benidorm balcony fall: Bury teen Jamie opens eyes after two weeks
articles.summary: Jamie, 17, has had two emergency operations since falling from a sixth-floor balcony on 10 November.
articles.body:
A teenager who fell from a sixth-floor hotel balcony in Spain has opened his eyes and responded to his relatives after spending nearly two weeks in intensive care, his family has said.

Jamie, 17, was seriously injured in Benidorm on 10 November and has had two emergency operations.

His family, from Bury in Greater Manchester, said doctors had been reducing Jamie's sedation and went on to say that he had responded to their voices and had followed instructions.

While the teenager's lungs are improving, he remains seriously ill, still requires support from a ventilator and faces further surgery, they said.

"After so many days of seeing him heavily sedated, we finally got to see those eyes open, see him looking at us, responding to our voices and following instructions," the family said.

"After nearly two weeks of worry, waiting and uncertainty, those moments meant more to us than we could ever put into words."

Jamie had been on holiday with his mum Gemma and her friends.

His aunt Lauren said the family did not know the circumstances which led to him falling from the balcony.

Describing how she felt when she learned what had happened, Lauren said it had been "the worst phone call of my life".

She described her close relationship with keen football fan Jamie and said they had spent time together at matches.

Following the fall, Jamie was initially treated in Benidorm before being transferred to a hospital in Alicante.

According to his family, surgeons inserted a stent to repair a ruptured artery and used an external metal frame to stabilise his severely fractured pelvis.

He also suffered broken legs and an arm, fractures to his chest and a punctured lung, according to a fundraising appeal set up by Lauren.

Further surgery on his pelvis had been postponed because of a lung infection.

Lauren has launched a £20,000 fundraising appeal to help cover costs not met by their insurance or charities, including bringing Jamie back to the UK and expenses for his family while he remains in hospital.

In their latest update, the family thanked people for their donations and messages of support.

The BBC has asked both the hotel and Spanish police about the incident.
